entries.clue: Concern with one about to leave – leaving partner in this? (8)

indicatorNotes.to leave: the letters named go away from the word they sit in

blocks.note: I = one, C = circa, about; these two letters leave SOLICITUDE

annotation.surface: Someone worried about a person on the point of walking out on their partner.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash splits wordplay from a definition by example: if you leave your partner, solitude is where you end up, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Walking out on a partner leaves you alone, in solitude.

entries.clue: Secure underwater line (4)

blocks.note: split as under + water: water is the SEA, and in a down entry the L goes under it

annotation.surface: Fastening a cable that runs along the seabed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Underwater' reads as one word, but it splits: L goes under SEA, which in a down entry means below it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sealing an envelope or a jar fastens it so nothing gets in or out.

entries.clue: Article buried by burrower endlessly turning up in soil (4)

indicatorNotes.buried by: the article is put inside the burrower
indicatorNotes.endlessly: the burrower loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down clue, the letters read upwards, reversed

blocks.note: a MOLE burrows; drop its last letter
A is the indefinite article, placed inside the reversed LOM

annotation.surface: An object buried by a mole, turning up in the earth.
annotation.walkthrough: The picture of a mole surfacing with something buried is a perfect disguise for the mole itself being the ingredient.
annotation.definitionFit: Loam is a fertile soil of clay, sand and humus.

entries.clue: University gone round by number about to get secure position (6)

indicatorNotes.gone round by: the letters that follow surround the university

annotation.surface: A university being toured by several people hoping for a permanent job.
annotation.walkthrough: Tenure is the permanent post an academic hopes for, so the university in the surface is part of the scene, not just a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Tenure is a permanent, secure appointment, especially in academia.

entries.clue: Running down daughter, is dad with anger unkind, wasting a bit of time? (13)

indicatorNotes.wasting: throws away the A from MEAN
indicatorNotes.bit of: only a small piece, the first letter, of time is taken

annotation.surface: A daughter complaining that her angry father is being mean and wasting time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wasting a bit of time' looks like one phrase; it splits into 'wasting a' acting on MEAN and 'bit of time' giving T.
annotation.definitionFit: Disparagement is the act of running someone down, belittling them.

entries.clue: Attempt to convey story about something refreshingly sweet? (6)

indicatorNotes.to convey: GO carries the story inside it

blocks.note: a tale is a story; reversed to ELAT inside GO

annotation.surface: Trying to tell a tale about a sweet treat.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as a description rather than a synonym: gelato is Italian ice cream.
annotation.definitionFit: Gelato is Italian ice cream, cold and sweet.

entries.clue: Finish with love, having spirited sort of marriage (8)

blocks.note: gamy (or gamey) = plucky, spirited, like a game bird

annotation.surface: Ending up in love and in a lively marriage.
annotation.walkthrough: Endogamy is marriage within one's own group or tribe; GAMY in the sense of spirited is the less familiar piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Endogamy is the custom of marrying within one's own group.

entries.clue: A cunning viewpoint that maths teacher may explain (5,5)

blocks.note: an angle on something is a viewpoint

annotation.surface: A crafty perspective a maths teacher might set out in class.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: an acute angle is one less than 90 degrees, the kind of thing taught in geometry.
annotation.definitionFit: An acute angle, under 90 degrees, is a basic idea a maths teacher explains.

entries.clue: Old writer’s English unchanged, words having magical effect (4,6)

blocks.note: a pen is a writer, with its apostrophe S

annotation.surface: An old author's English left as it was, his words working magic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer' is the pen, not a person. Open sesame is the password from Ali Baba that opens the robbers' cave.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Open sesame' is the magic phrase that opens the cave in Ali Baba.

entries.clue: Odd man is sane, as shown in medical record (9)

indicatorNotes.Odd: the letters are put in a strange order

annotation.surface: A strange man's case notes declare him sane.
annotation.walkthrough: The medical surface is apt: an anamnesis is a patient's case history, recalled for the doctor.
annotation.definitionFit: An anamnesis is a patient's medical history as recounted.

entries.clue: Lack of courage that is evident in wormy types (13)

annotation.definition: Lack of courage that is evident in wormy types

blocks.clueFragment: that is evident in wormy types
blocks.note: the surface means feeble, worm-like people; the setter also means real worms, invertebrates with no spine at all

annotation.surface: Cowardice shown by people who are worms.
annotation.walkthrough: Wormy types are both feeble people and actual worms, which literally have no spine.
annotation.definitionFit: Spinelessness is lack of courage, and also, literally, having no backbone.

entries.clue: Trick by five hundred members of religious sect (5)

annotation.definitionNote: DRUSE is a plural collective name here, matching 'members'
annotation.surface: A scam worked by five hundred members of a sect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trick by five hundred' puts RUSE beside D, with D going first. The Druse (Druze) are a religious community of Lebanon, Syria and Israel.
annotation.definitionFit: The Druse (or Druze) are an esoteric religious sect of the Middle East.

entries.clue: The latest answer involves this action in a river (8,4)

blocks.note: the definition: the most recent report

blocks.clueFragment: answer involves this action in a river
blocks.note: a riddle rather than wordplay: breaking is also something water does in a river, over rocks or through its banks

annotation.surface: A puzzle answer that involves some action taking place in a river.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is loose: rivers break (over rocks, through their banks), so the answer 'involves' a river action. 'The latest' reads as an adjective on 'answer' but stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Breaking news is a story just coming in, so 'The latest' names it by its freshness.

entries.clue: Agricultural land to flourish, absorbing warmth with minimum of frost (10)

indicatorNotes.absorbing: WIELD takes the other letters inside it
indicatorNotes.minimum of: only the smallest part, the first letter, of frost

blocks.note: to flourish a sword is to wield it
first letter of frost; HEAT and F go inside WIELD

annotation.surface: Farmland thriving because it has warmth and hardly any frost.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flourish' reads as crops thriving, but here it means brandishing, as with a weapon: WIELD.
annotation.definitionFit: A wheatfield is farmland sown with wheat.

entries.clue: Activity of artist, showing concern about Newcastle? (10)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' in its sense of around, so CARING is wrapped around TOON

blocks.note: the Toon is the local nickname for Newcastle upon Tyne, from Geordie for town

annotation.surface: An artist who worries about the city of Newcastle.
annotation.walkthrough: Newcastle is a city in north-east England, and locals call it the Toon; the question mark flags the nickname.
annotation.definitionFit: Cartooning, drawing cartoons, is an artist's activity.

entries.clue: House with a sign of something wrong that fraudster perpetrates? (4)

blocks.note: a cross, the sign marking something wrong

annotation.surface: A house showing signs of a crime committed by a swindler.
annotation.walkthrough: X is the teacher's mark for a wrong answer. The definition describes rather than names: a hoax is what a fraudster carries out.
annotation.definitionFit: A hoax is a deception, the kind of thing a fraudster pulls off.

entries.clue: Sad men could do this to atone (4,6)

blocks.note: the surface means sorry, remorseful men; the setter means the six letters S, A, D, M, E, N
the surface means they could put things right; the setter means those letters could MAKE the word AMENDS

annotation.surface: Sorrowful men who could make up for their wrongs.
annotation.walkthrough: The letters of SAD MEN can be made into AMENDS, so sad men could literally make AMENDS.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: making amends means putting right a wrong you did, which is what atoning is.

entries.clue: Fibrous products obtained from sewers? (8)

blocks.note: the surface suggests muck made of fibre clogging pipes; the setter means loops of thread
sewers reads as drains; the setter means people who sew

annotation.surface: Fibrous waste recovered from drains.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sewers' looks like drains, but read it as people who sew; what they produce, in thread, is stitches.
annotation.definitionFit: Stitches are loops of thread, fibrous things made by those who sew.

entries.clue: Social worker is embracing these opposite types (10)

indicatorNotes.embracing: to embrace is to hug, so IS wraps its arms around THESE

blocks.note: the ant is a social insect and a worker
used as it stands, inside IS

annotation.surface: A social worker hugging people who are complete opposites.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a job; it is an ANT, a social insect that works.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an antithesis is the direct opposite of something, so antitheses are opposite types.

entries.clue: Alluring sparkle exuding energy (4)

indicatorNotes.exuding: the E is let out of GLEAM

annotation.surface: An attractive shine that radiates vitality.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exuding energy' suggests radiance pouring out; here it means letting the E out of GLEAM.
annotation.definitionFit: Glam, short for glamorous, means alluring.

entries.clue: What river rises, producing foam? (6)

indicatorNotes.rises: in a down clue, the letters read upwards, reversed

blocks.note: the Tees is a river in north-east England

annotation.surface: Asking what a rising river does as it churns into foam.
annotation.walkthrough: EHTEES read upwards gives SEETHE. 'What' looks like a question word introducing the clue; it is the interjection EH.
annotation.definitionFit: Water that seethes bubbles and foams.

entries.clue: Finer monster upsetting chaps living on the edge? (12)

indicatorNotes.upsetting: the letters are overturned into a new order

annotation.surface: A superior monster frightening daredevils.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Living on the edge' suggests thrill-seekers; the question mark flags the literal sense of settlers at a frontier.
annotation.definitionFit: Frontiersmen live on the frontier, the edge of settled land.

entries.clue: Bird – one beginning to breed on island (4)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: only the first letter of breed
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, the earlier pieces sit on top of IS

annotation.surface: A bird starting to breed on an island.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true, since seabirds do nest on islands, which makes the dash-separated definition easy to overlook.
annotation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-billed wading bird.

entries.clue: Trade very limited? Then pack up (4)

indicatorNotes.limited: very is cut down to its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of very; V is also the standard abbreviation
to pack up is to stop, end

annotation.surface: Business is poor, so shut up shop.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark breaks the clue in two; 'pack up' here means stop working, not fill a suitcase.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: vending is selling goods, which is trading.

entries.clue: Woman to change husband (5)

annotation.surface: A wife set on swapping her husband.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Woman' at the start of a clue usually signals a female first name built from pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Edith is one woman's first name, so 'Woman' stands for any such name.

entries.clue: Nasty tear at front of furniture item that can be repaired? (9)

indicatorNotes.Nasty: the letters of tear are turned into a new order
indicatorNotes.at front of: the jumbled letters go before TABLE

blocks.note: a table is an item of furniture

annotation.surface: A bad rip on a piece of furniture that might be mended.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is loose, hence the question mark: treatable usually means curable, here stretched to fixable.
annotation.definitionFit: Something treatable can be remedied or put right.

entries.clue: Review with snide remark is not British (6)

blocks.note: a dig is a snide remark

annotation.surface: A critic's write-up containing a snide jab, which is not British in tone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not British' tells you to use a foreign word, here French: est means is.
annotation.definitionFit: A digest condenses material into a survey of it, as in Reader's Digest, so it serves as a review.

entries.clue: Somehow sad, blue inside, being defamed (8)

annotation.definitionNote: ASPERSED is a past participle; 'being defamed' stands for it in a passive sense

indicatorNotes.Somehow: sad is rearranged in some way
indicatorNotes.inside: the blue goes into the rearranged letters

blocks.note: SAD rearranged, split around the blue
perse is a greyish-blue colour, placed inside AS…D

annotation.surface: Feeling down and low after being badmouthed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like part of the sadness; it is a colour, the rare PERSE.
annotation.definitionFit: To asperse someone is to slander or defame them.
